hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 21
hunts.subtitle: Quail opens today, the weather turns tomorrow, and the rabbits have not been consulted on either.

rules.title: Today's rules at a glance
items: **Quail opens today**, Nov 21. It is a regular small-game season: no HIP or federal stamp, but carry your license.
**Crow is open today** (Wed, Fri, Sat only). Doves and snipe are open if the NCWRC dates still read the same when you check.
**Migratory birds need HIP certification and a plug** that holds only 3 shells total.
**Hunter orange is required.** Deer gun season stays open for others until Jan 1. Bear season ends Nov 22.
Clocks are on standard time now. The next change is Sunday Mar 14, 2027 (spring forward).
rules.note: Confirm seasons and bag limits in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go.

items: Walk-in: low near **40F**, light and variable wind, partly cloudy. Another weather page disagreed on the low, so bring a layer.
9 am: no hourly figure was listed. The daily high is near **70F**, so it warms fast after sunrise.
Wind: **northeast 5 to 10 mph** for the day. Gusts were not listed.
Sky: more clouds than sun. Rain chance about **6 percent** Saturday. **Rain is forecast Sunday** (a coastal storm is possible).
Sunrise **6:51 am**. Legal light **6:21 am** (both calculated).
Moon: **waxing gibbous, about 90 percent** (calculated), full early next week. Moonrise and moonset were not found.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a mild morning with weather coming in tomorrow tends to push squirrels and rabbits to feed hard early, so expect the best movement from about 6:45 to 9:00 and less waiting for the sun.
conditions.hours_note: No hour-by-hour table for Saturday was available, so the hourly chart is left out.

wind.label: NE 5 to 10 (daily forecast; hourly detail not listed)

in_season.tip: Feed trees with fresh cuttings. Mild air means they move early.
Thick pine and holly edges. Practice the solo kick-and-wait push (see skill).
No covey has been seen here. Bonus only. Listen at first light.
Watch the sky for flight lines. Shoot only with a clear sky shot to the north.
Swamp edges and mud flats. Needs HIP and a 3-shell plug.

in_season: Raccoon and opossum are open. Take only a sure, close shot.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.
Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Thicket Edge Seat
plan.why: New spot today: the **north edge of the thickest pine-and-holly cluster, where it meets more open woods, about 50 paces west of the north end of the loop trail**. Sit against a wide pine facing **northwest**. The northeast breeze crosses from your right, so your scent drifts away behind your left shoulder, off the lit trunks ahead. The rising sun comes up behind your right shoulder. Rabbits sit in the thick cover at your back and edge, and squirrels cut cones in the pines in front. After the seated hour you walk the same thicket edge for a solo rabbit push. Every shot goes between WNW and NNE with a trunk or the ground behind the animal.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, about 25 minutes before legal light. Red light only. 20 steps, stop 10 seconds. Gun unloaded.
Reach the loop trail's north end, then walk west along the thicket edge. Sit against the widest pine, facing NW. Load #4 with the plug in. Red light off.
Legal light. Stay still. Listen for a quail covey whistle and crow calls. Scan trunks 20 to 40 yards out from WNW round to NNE.
Sunrise. Watch for cone scales falling and tail flicks in the pines. Run the backstop check on each squirrel.
Seated hour done. Mild air keeps squirrels moving, so take a sure shot if one offers. Mark any fall on a trunk.
Unload and start the rabbit push along the thicket edge, heading northeast into the wind. Kick, then wait 30 seconds. Shots N, W, or E only.
Work south along the loop to the feed bins, sunny edge of cover. Shoot N or W only. Never toward the field SE.
Unload at the bins. Count shells. Walk out by the main trail, doing the land task.
Unloaded and out. Real hunting ends here.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in). Good for squirrel and rabbit to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for a close rabbit, a quail flush, or a dove.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot carried.**
**Choke: Modified.** Fine for everything today.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on still squirrels only, with a trunk or the ground behind.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
Quail and rabbits flush close and loud. Hold the shot until the bird or rabbit is clear and north of you.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game on the property. Grays work oaks, hickories, and hollies. A fox squirrel may show in the pines.
With mild air they feed early. Expect movement from about 6:45 and a strong window to 9:00.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards. Aim at the head and neck of a squirrel on a trunk.
With the .22: head only, with wood or ground behind.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Mark the fall against a trunk.

details.title: Call: bark chatter
steps: Make a short, dry chuk-chuk with your tongue against the roof of your mouth.
Do it three times, 2 seconds apart, then stay still for 5 minutes.
Use it only from the seat. A squirrel often answers or leans out to look.

after: Tip: cone scales falling onto leaves mean a squirrel is feeding right now. Look straight up the trunk.
Tip: a squirrel that circles a trunk to hide returns in about 2 minutes. Wait with the gun ready.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails live in the thick pine and holly edges and near the feed bins. They sit tight and flush only when you are close.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards, aimed at the head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: kick and wait
steps: Walk a few steps, kick a brush pile or thick clump, then stand still for 30 seconds.
A rabbit that bolts often stops after 15 to 20 yards to look back.
Look for the black eye and the ear line, not the whole body.
Shoot when it stops and the ground is behind it.

after: Tip: wear gloves to clean rabbits. Discard any rabbit with white spots on the liver.

animals.name: Quail (opens today)
paragraphs: Northern bobwhite. No covey has been seen on the property, so treat quail as a pleasant surprise, not the plan.
If a covey exists it holds in the thickest low cover at the edge of open ground and flushes all at once with a loud whirr.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 in the right pocket is the quail load. #4 in the gun will also work at 20 to 30 yards.
Pick ONE bird. Do not shoot into the brown of the covey.
Shoot only if the bird flies north, west, or east. Never swing south.

details.title: Technique: listen first
steps: At first light, stand still near thick edge cover and listen for the two-note covey call.
If you hear it, mark the direction. Walk slowly toward it and stop every few steps.
Let the covey flush, then swing through one bird and follow through.

after: Tip: take no quail from a covey that flushes toward the south or the field. Let them go.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows pass over the swamp and pine tops in the morning. Saturday is an open day.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 25 to 35 yards on a bird coming in.
Shoot only when the sky north of you is clear.

after: Tip: a crow cawing hard and circling is mobbing something, often an owl or a hawk. Watch the treetops.

animals.name: Dove and snipe (opportunity)
paragraphs: Doves may cross the swamp edge or the wood line. Snipe use wet mud flats near the beaver lodge. Both need HIP and a plug.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 20 to 30 yards.
Shoot only a bird flying north, west, or east, with a clear sky behind it.

after: Tip: a snipe flushes with a scratchy call and zig-zags. Wait for it to straighten.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night along the swamp and around the feed bins. At first light the last ones head for hollow trees.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Touch the eye with a stick to confirm it is dead. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: a dark, wet track on pale mud is fresh.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season is open through Nov 22, so you may hear other hunters. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Reading rabbit cover and the solo kick-and-wait push
skill.principle: A rabbit hides until you are almost on it, then runs a short circle. Find the cover it likes, move slowly, and give it a reason to break where you can shoot safely.

sections.title: Read the cover
steps: Look for thick, low cover with a sunny side: briars, pine and holly edges, brush piles.
Look for a form: a shallow oval pressed in the grass or leaves, about the size of a fist.
Look for clipped twigs cut at a clean 45 degree angle and round, dry pellets.
Look for a run: a thin, bare trail through the cover at rabbit height.

sections.title: The solo push
steps: Walk the edge into the wind, 3 slow steps at a time.
At a thick clump or brush pile, kick it hard and step back.
Stand still for 30 seconds. Most rabbits sit, then bolt, then stop to look back.
When it stops, check the backstop, then shoot. If it runs south, let it go.

sections.title: Safe lines on this land
steps: Push so the cover lies to your N, W, or E, never to the south.
At the feed bins, shoot N or W only. The field is SE.
Unload before you cross logs or the swamp edge.

details.title: Why the pause works
paragraphs: A rabbit that has been kicked loses nerve when you go quiet. The pause makes it run, and a running rabbit often stops once to check you. That stop is your shot.

skill.checkpoint: Find one form or run today and note which side of the cover it faced. Send it with a note: message.

land.intro: Find where the rabbits live and how they move, using their sign.
steps: On the walk out, look along the thicket edge and the loop for clipped twigs, pellets, forms, and runs.
Find the 2 thickest brush piles or clumps. Pace each from the Junction.
Note which side of the cover gets morning sun.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: pellets and a form 30 paces east of the loop's north end, sunny side, run heads north.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between WNW and NNE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal. Sky shots at crow, dove, or quail only to the north.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season and bear season are open for other hunters.
Quail and rabbits flush close and fast. Keep the muzzle north and your finger outside the guard until the shot is sure.
Unload before crossing logs, the swamp edge, or open ground.
It is about 40F at walk-in and near 70F by afternoon. Wear layers you can open.
